questiontext.text:
A [[if test="is(ix=1)"]]delivery motorbike[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=2)"]]laptop[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=3)"]]lorry[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=4)"]]posho mill[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=5)"]]photocopier[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=6)"]]tractor[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=7)"]]solar water pump[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=8)"]]tuk-tuk[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=9)"]]printer[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=10)"]]matatu engine[[/if]] costs Ksh \({@ksh(P)@}\). Give a yearly rate of depreciation (reducing balance) for which it is worth less than half its price after \({@n@}\) years, but not after \({@n-1@}\) years. Many answers are correct; you may use one decimal place.

[[input:ansr]] % [[validation:ansr]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Half the price is Ksh \({@ksh(half)@}\). Try a rate and work out the value after \({@n-1@}\) and after \({@n@}\) years.

For example, with \({@tmid@}\%\) the multiplier is \({@dd(1-tmid/100)@}\): after \({@n-1@}\) years the value is Ksh \({@ksh(vtm)@}\), still at least half, and after \({@n@}\) years Ksh \({@ksh(vt)@}\), below half. So \({@tmid@}\%\) works.

By trial, to one decimal place the rates that work are from \({@dispdp(float((floor(float(1000*(1-2^(-1/n))))+1)/10),1)@}\%\) to \({@dispdp(float(floor(float(1000*(1-2^(-1/(n-1)))))/10),1)@}\%\). A smaller rate is too slow; a bigger rate takes the value below half a year too early.

questiondescription.text:
Commercial Arithmetic III: choosing a rate of depreciation

Grade 12 CBE Essential 2.4 (c): Find a yearly rate of reducing-balance depreciation that takes a value below half its price in a given year but not before.

Essential

This question is original to this project.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Essential Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: After \({@n-1@}\) years it is worth Ksh \({@ksh(vm)@}\), after \({@n@}\) years Ksh \({@ksh(vn)@}\): below half (Ksh \({@ksh(half)@}\)) only after year \({@n@}\).
A rate of depreciation is between \(0\%\) and \(100\%\).
Too fast: with \({@ansr@}\%\) it is already below half after \({@n-1@}\) years (Ksh \({@ksh(vm)@}\)). Try a smaller rate.
\({@dispdp(float(50/n),2)@}\%\) would halve it only if it lost the same amount every year. With reducing balance the losses shrink, so you need a bigger rate.

falsefeedback.text: Too slow: after \({@n@}\) years it is still worth Ksh \({@ksh(vn)@}\), more than half. Try a bigger rate.

qtest.description: Correct: a rate inside the interval
